newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks weak but off lows in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks weak but off lows in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened weak on Friday morning in line with other world markets and due to fears of an uptrend in interest rates.
But brokers and analysts held differing views on the market's near-term outlook.

"This is likely to be the last round of the sell-off," said Andrew To, dealing director at OSK Asia Securities. "If the index falls to 12,000 that will be a 2,000-point correction from the top, a 14 percent correction."
The Hang Seng Index was 82 points lower at 12,389 after 30 minutes of trade on robust turnover of HK$1.76 billion.
"Wall Street has only fallen about 5.0 percent (from its peak). The Hong Kong market is overreacting," To added.
The Dow Jones Industrials fell 57.40 or 0.83 percent to 6,820.28 following comments made by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan. He signalled that the central bank was inching towards raising interest rates.
On a technical view, support lies at 12,200 and 12,000, but analysts are not sure how strong these are.
"These levels are rough levels," said analyst Ted Chen of Technical Data Inc. "I'm putting major support in a band of 11,900 to 12,200."
The finance sector led the market down. Banking giant HSBC Holdings lost HK$3.50 to HK$174.00 before rising to HK$176.00, off only HK$1.50.

Red chip Shanghai Industrial was the next largest loser and second most actively traded issue after HSBC. The share shed HK$1.80 to HK$31.90, then recovered somewhat to trade HK$0.90 lower at HK$32.80.
March Hang Seng Index futures moved in line with the cash market. The March contract dipped to a low of 12,335 at the open but quickly regained that ground to trade 15 points higher at 12,415.
